pr_title: NFSv3 and NFSv4 fixes and improvements
pr_body:
## Description
NFSv3 and NFSv4 fixes and improvements:

- Fixes session expiration due insufficient keep alive interval (NFSv4 only).
- Fixes attempt to reuse cached but expired NFS contexts (NFSv4 only).
- Fixes crash when read Blu-Ray BDMV structures and some optional files not exist (NFSv3 & NFSv4).
- Use 128K read/write chunk size in NFSv4  (NFSv4 servers do not enforce or limit to any specific value).
- Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/22862
- Fixes https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/22714#issuecomment-1439719284

## Motivation and context
Due to the big differences between NFSv3 and NFSv4, certain changes are necessary, especially everything related to time outs and keep alive:

> NFSv3 is stateless. That effectively means that the NFS server (ONTAP) doesn't keep track of which filesystems are mounted, by whom, or which locks are truly in place. Tracking NFS client state is not part of the NFSv3 standard.
> 
> In contrast, NFSv4 is stateful. The NFSv4 server tracks which clients are using which filesystems, which files exist, which files and/or regions of files are locked, etc. This means there needs to be regular communication between an NFSv4 server to keep the state data current.

https://community.netapp.com/t5/Tech-ONTAP-Blogs/NFSv3-and-NFSv4-What-s-the-difference/ba-p/441316

> The client queries the server's "lease_time" attribute. (Default 90s on Linux.)
> Normal filesystem activity starts. The client ensures that it sends one rpc (may be some sort of no-op) at least every lease_time, to reassure the server that it's still active.

> NFSv3 also has the notion of grace periods and reclaim flags on lock requests. The main differences are:
> there's no lease time, and clients aren't required to poll the server regularly.

https://linux-nfs.org/wiki/index.php/NFS_lock_recovery_notes

## How has this been tested?
Runtime Windows x64 and Android (Shield). 
As NFSv4 server used Synology NAS (DSM 7.1.1) Indeed, it has been proven that it has 90s "lease_time".
Tested NFSv3 and NFSv4, tested and reproduced all issues mentioned.

## What is the effect on users?
- Fixes random `NFS4ERR_EXPIRED` errors at open files any time.
- Fixes video playback stalls and closes after pause due insufficient keep alive of NFSv4 session.
- Fixes crash opening Blu-Ray folders (BDMV) if some optional files not present (very common).
- Fixes slow NFSv4 read when not using file cache due very small read chunk size.

## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:

Video playback stops due to unreliable NFSv4 mount



## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:

Video playback show not prematurely end

Video playback stops seemingly due to read access to file changing while playback is occurring due to NFSv4 mount

128K has been chosen (and should be fine for all) because 128K is already used in NFSv3 and also when FileCahe is used with NFSv4.

This code force to use default 128K chunk size when source reports 0:

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/56b88b2bf5d82fd2b2feb4df4b35f81e70ca1b89/xbmc/filesystem/FileCache.cpp#L138-L144

File chunk size is a bit chaotic because is hardcoded in many places:

https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/56b88b2bf5d82fd2b2feb4df4b35f81e70ca1b89/xbmc/filesystem/File.cpp#L119

> There is already chunksize as advancedsetting

This is chunk size for FileCahe only

We can create a new setting for NFS only (when is not used in combination with FileCache)

As long term FileCache should have their GUI settings...
and SMB their chunk size in SMB GUI settings
and NFS their chunk size in NFS GUI settings

yes, it's cache only, so won't work when caching is disabled.

adding this in a followup PR is fine for me.
I'm surprised clang-format doesn't trip up on this.
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/docs/CODE_GUIDELINES.md#6-scoping
Shouldn't we early return here to skip the SEEK_SET below?
Because this value can be changed is why I avoided adjusting the timeouts in the first place.

But Linux default (nfs-kernel-server) is 90s. This is so....

6 minutes does NOT work. If you want to use 6 minutes because "avoid change here" then you need submit patch to Linux kernel

Wouldn't an advanced setting for this purpose be better (while keeping the sane defaults)?
I assume there's no easy way to get those values from the server

> I assume there's no easy way to get those values from the server

In fact, the spec says that clients should get the lease_time from the server:

> The client queries the server's "lease_time" attribute. (Default 90s on Linux.)

https://linux-nfs.org/wiki/index.php/NFS_lock_recovery_notes

But we are limited to what `libnfs` offers and I haven't found a way to get this (note that this is "new" in NFSv4 and v4 support in libnfs is very limited and NFSv4.1 is unsupported).

Anyway 45s keep alive interval should work in all cases because common values are 90s (default), 120s or 60s.

30s or less is discouraged.
Maybe @sahlberg know more about the leasing period. It would be nice if we could just query it.

I also think that it is necessary to clarify here that the keep alive that we have implemented (it was already in NFSv3) are not to keep the NFS server's session active (this concept simply did not exist in NFSv3) but rather to prevent the hard disk from stopping spin up and go into hibernation when the video is paused for several minutes.

It is true that now with NFSv4 the same keep alive works for both.

The keep alive for NFS session does not need to read data from the hard drive, it just sends a RENEW command. On the other hand, to keep the hard drive spinning, it is necessary to read something...

> The client may renew its lease with use of the RENEW operation or implicitly by use of other operations (primarily READ).

https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/2.1.0?topic=control-locking-in-nfs-version-4
Are positive error codes allowed?

only `ret == 0` is open successfully, then `ret != 0` is open FAILED which is precisely what we want to detect here

```
/*
 * Sync open(<filename>)
 * Function returns
 *      0 : The operation was successful. *nfsfh is filled in.
 * -errno : The command failed.
 */
EXTERN int nfs_open(struct nfs_context *nfs, const char *path, int flags,
                    struct nfsfh **nfsfh);
```
Why do these other values need to be adjusted?
Because context "expires" when time of inactivity is greater than server's "lease_time"

Current solution is:

CONTEXT_TIMEOUT = 6 minutes
But expires in 90s then when someone opens a file after 90s `nfs_open` fails with NFS4ERR_EXPIRED but is retry with https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/commit/9dc30e83c830d379c063eaf3a4a64a9fb57ca782


New solution is:

Discard expired contexts so `nfs_open` should never fail and should never retry...
I imagine you changed this to debug because it's a bit spammy with the faster keep alive.
